chains.title: HNF4A binds ref G at a cryptic distal element and alters CYP7A1
chains.element: cryptic distal HNF4A site in an intronic/intergenic segment

links.claim: HNF4A is proposed to bind the ref G allele more strongly than the alt T allele. No positive QBiC-SELEX, ChIP-seq, MPRA, or reporter evidence supports this. QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked because no QBiC-SELEX row or TF lookup was provided. E07 reports no ENCODE HNF4A ChIP-seq peak containing rs7001688, although absence can also reflect no HNF4A experiment in the relevant biosample; this remains a low-confidence motif hypothesis.

E01 places rs7001688 as an intron_variant/intergenic variant with no regulatory feature, and E03 reports no overlapping cCRE; the nearest cCRE is 1544 bp away. These support only the genomic location and absence of an annotated cCRE, not the existence of a functional cryptic HNF4A element.

CYP7A1 is proposed as a long-range target because it is the nearest cholesterol/bile-acid gene among the listed genes, but E02 gives only distance to TSS (926.8 kb downstream) and no chromatin-contact, eQTL, or perturbation evidence links rs7001688 to CYP7A1.

The proposed cellular context is Hep3B2.1-7 hepatocyte (DepMap ACH-000625), as given in the case expression context; no cited evidence shows HNF4A expression, chromatin accessibility, or allele-specific regulatory activity at this locus in that cell type.

If ref G increases HNF4A binding and HNF4A activates CYP7A1, then the alt T allele would reduce CYP7A1 and raise LDL cholesterol. This direction is speculative: HNF4A can activate or repress, and no evidence links rs7001688 to CYP7A1 expression or LDL cholesterol.
